executiveSummary: Available reporting indicates two significant logistics-facing cyber incidents with direct maritime relevance over the period: (1) North Carolina Ports experienced a confirmed cyberattack that triggered contingency procedures and manual processing across multiple facilities, with U.S. Coast Guard engagement; the port reported the incident was "contained." View Article CEVA Logistics, a CMA CGM Group subsidiary, disclosed a cyberattack that disrupted European contract logistics operations at eight warehouses, delaying shipments and creating downstream supply-chain friction for maritime customers. View Article

descriptions: Observed behavior (plain language): Intrusion into enterprise IT environments causing disruption to port administrative workflows and warehouse contract logistics operations.

Potential behaviors (inferred, not confirmed): Unauthorized access to business applications, disruption of fulfillment systems, and forced manual fallback. A formal ATT&CK mapping could not be confirmed from the supplied sources.
